metadata.imageAlt: Aggregate-demand graph with solid AD0 and dashed AD1 to its right on numbered price-level and real-GDP axes.

metadata.imageAlt: Short-run aggregate-supply graph with solid AS0 and dashed AS1 above and left of it on numbered axes.

metadata.imageAlt: Supply-and-demand shift graph with labeled prices and quantities.

metadata.imageAlt: Aggregate-demand multiplier graph with AD1, AD2, and AD3 shifting progressively right at a fixed price level P, corresponding to output levels Y1, Y2, and Y3.
metadata.graphDescription: The horizontal axis is real output Y and the vertical axis is the price level P. A horizontal line at price level P crosses three downward-sloping aggregate-demand curves. AD1 intersects at output Y1, AD2 lies to the right and intersects at Y2, and AD3 lies farther right and intersects at Y3, so Y1 is less than Y2, which is less than Y3.

metadata.imageAlt: Aggregate-demand multiplier graph with AD1, AD2, and AD3 shifting progressively right at a fixed price level P, corresponding to output levels Y1, Y2, and Y3.

metadata.imageAlt: U.S. dollar market with downward-sloping demand D0 and upward-sloping supply S0 intersecting at A.
metadata.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar. The horizontal axis is the quantity of U.S. dollars exchanged. Downward-sloping D0 and upward-sloping S0 intersect at A, quantity 100 and exchange rate 1.0.

metadata.imageAlt: Dollar demand shifts right from D0 to D1 while upward-sloping supply S0 remains fixed.
metadata.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Demand shifts right from solid D0 to dashed D1 along unchanged upward-sloping S0. Equilibrium moves from A at quantity 100 and rate 1.0 to B at quantity 150 and rate 1.2.

metadata.imageAlt: Upward-sloping dollar supply shifts right from S0 to S1 along demand D0.
metadata.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Demand D0 is unchanged while supply shifts right from solid S0 to dashed S1. Equilibrium moves from A at quantity 100 and rate 1.0 to B at quantity 150 and rate 0.8.

metadata.imageAlt: Dollar demand and upward-sloping supply both shift right, from D0 and S0 to D1 and S1.
metadata.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Demand and supply both shift right. Original equilibrium A is quantity 100 and rate 1.0; final equilibrium B is quantity 200 and rate 1.0. Solid curves are D0 and S0; dashed curves are D1 and S1. D1 crosses S0 at approximately quantity 150 and rate 1.2; D0 crosses S1 at approximately quantity 150 and rate 0.8. These two crossings have no point labels or dashed coordinate guides.

metadata.imageAlt: Conceptual dollar market showing demand shifting right from D0 to D1 with supply S0 unchanged.
metadata.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Dashed demand D1 lies right of solid D0 while upward-sloping S0 is unchanged. The new intersection is above and right of the original intersection. No numerical ticks are shown.

metadata.imageAlt: Conceptual dollar market showing upward-sloping supply shifting right from S0 to S1 with demand D0 unchanged.
metadata.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. metadata.imageAlt: Conceptual dollar market showing demand and upward-sloping supply both shifting right.
metadata.graphDescription: The vertical axis is foreign currency per U.S. dollar and the horizontal axis is the quantity of dollars exchanged. Demand shifts right from D0 to D1 and supply shifts right from S0 to S1. The displayed shifts raise equilibrium quantity while leaving the exchange rate at the same vertical position. No numerical ticks are shown.

metadata.imageAlt: Mankiw-model dollar market with vertical supply shifting left from S0 equals NCO0 to S1 equals NCO1 along D0 equals NX0.

metadata.imageAlt: Conceptual Mankiw-model dollar market with vertical supply shifting left from S0 equals NCO0 to S1 equals NCO1.

metadata.imageAlt: Phillips-curve graph with two downward-sloping short-run Phillips curves and a vertical long-run Phillips curve at unemployment rate U2, with labeled points a through d.

SRPC1 is the lower/left downward-sloping curve and SRPC2 is the higher/right downward-sloping curve. Point a is at U1/I2 on SRPC1, point b is at U2/I2 where SRPC2 meets the LRPC, point c is at U2/I1 where SRPC1 meets the LRPC, and point d is at U3/I1 on SRPC2. metadata.imageAlt: Phillips-curve graph with two downward-sloping short-run Phillips curves, labeled unemployment rates U1 through U4, inflation rates I1 through I4, and points a through f.
metadata.graphDescription: The horizontal axis is unemployment rate and the vertical axis is inflation rate.
